entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 63 Is 63:1-19 . Messiah Coming as the Avenger, in Answer to His People's Prayers. Messiah, approaching Jerusalem after having avenged His people on His and their enemies, is represented under imagery taken from the destruction of "Edom," the type of the last and most bitter foes of God and His people (see Is 34:5 , &c.). 1. Who-- the question of the prophet in prophetic vision. dyed-- scarlet with blood ( Is 63:2 , 3 ; Re 19:13 ). Bozrah-- (See on Is 34:6 ). travelling-- rather, stately; literally, "throwing back the head" [Gesenius]. speak in righteousness-- answer of Messiah. I, who have in faithfulness given a promise of deliverance, am now about to fulfil it. Rather, speak of righteousness ( Is 45:19 ; 46:13 ); salvation being meant as the result of His "righteousness" [Maurer]. save-- The same Messiah that destroys the unbeliever saves the believer.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9494"/><div sID="gen16558" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9494"/>2. The prophet asks why His garments are "dyed" and "red."<div eID="gen16558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16559" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">winefat--</hi>rather, the "wine-press," wherein the grapes were trodden with the feet; the juice would stain the garment of him who trod them (<reference osisRef="Rev.14.19">Re 14:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.20">20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.15">19:15</reference>). The image was appropriate, as the country round Bozrah abounded in grapes. This final blow inflicted by Messiah and His armies (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.13-Rev.19.15">Re 19:13-15</reference>) shall decide His claim to the kingdoms usurped by Satan, and by the "beast," to whom Satan delegates his power. It will be a day of judgment to the hostile Gentiles, as His first coming was a day of judgment to the unbelieving Jews. <div eID="gen16559" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9500"/><div sID="gen16573" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9500"/><hi type="bold">8. he--</hi>Jehovah "said," that is, thought, in choosing them as His covenant-people; so "said" (<reference osisRef="Ps.95.10">Psa 95:10</reference>). Not that God was ignorant that the Jews would not keep faith with Him; but God is here said, according to human modes of thought to say within Himself what He might naturally have expected, as the result of His goodness to the Jews; thus the enormity of their unnatural perversity is the more vividly set forth.<div eID="gen16573" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16574" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lie--</hi>prove false to Me (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.44.17">Psa 44:17</reference>).<div eID="gen16574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16575" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">so--</hi>in virtue of His having chosen them, He became their Saviour. So the "therefore" (<reference osisRef="Jer.31.33">Jr 31:33</reference>). His eternal choice is the ground of His actually saving men (<reference osisRef="Eph.1.3">Ep 1:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.4">4</reference>). <div eID="gen16575" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9501"/><div sID="gen16576" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9501"/><hi type="bold">9. he was afflicted--</hi>English Version reads the Hebrew as the Keri (Margin), does, "There was affliction to Him." entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9511"/><div sID="gen16604" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9511"/><hi type="bold">19. thine ... never--</hi>rather, "We are Thine from of old; Thou barest not rule over them" [Barnes]. Lowth translates, "We for long have been as those over whom Thou hast not ruled, who are not called by Thy name"; "for long" thus stands in contrast to "but a little while" (<reference osisRef="Isa.63.18">Is 63:18</reference>). But the analogy of <reference osisRef="Isa.63.18">Is 63:18</reference> makes it likely that the first clause in this verse refers to the Jews, and the second to their foes, as English Version and Barnes translate it. The Jews' foes are aliens who have unjustly intruded into the Lord's heritage. <chapter eID="Isa.63"/>

navigation_sections.title: CHAPTER 63
navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 63 Is 63:1-19 . Messiah Coming as the Avenger, in Answer to His People's Prayers. Messiah, approaching Jerusalem after having avenged His people on His and their enemies, is represented under imagery taken from the destruction of "Edom," the type of the last and most bitter foes of God and His people (see Is 34:5 , &c.).
